subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should the remaining work stay scoped to a live-reproduced Telegram ingress/concurrency fix, or should maintainers approve a broader timeout/defaults redesign covering provider fallback, launchd/threadpool, DNS, and watchdog behavior?
rationale: The credible remaining problem crosses channel delivery, provider fallback, run timeouts, and operator-facing defaults, and source inspection alone cannot choose the compatibility-safe fix boundary.

options.title: Require live repro, then split narrow fixes
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, reproduce the four-agent Telegram timeout pattern on current main, and implement only the surfaces the repro proves.

options.title: Treat fallback mitigation as enough
options.body: Close or downgrade after the terminal-abort cascade mitigation, accepting that the original Telegram concurrency bottleneck is not proven fixed.

options.title: Approve broad defaults redesign
options.body: Proceed with a larger design covering Telegram sink decoupling plus launchd, DNS, threadpool, or watchdog defaults, accepting higher compatibility and operator-impact risk.

recommendation.title: Require live repro, then split narrow fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, reproduce the four-agent Telegram timeout pattern on current main, and implement only the surfaces the repro proves.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans Telegram runner and agent fallback behavior, and the existing issue review routes that current-main boundary decision to vincentkoc.
